summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic pancreatitis and sphincter of Oddi dysfunction was admitted for recurrent epigastric pain radiating to the back, associated with nausea and vomiting, consistent with prior pancreatitis flares. Lipase was mildly elevated to 103, and liver tests were normal. She was managed conservatively with NPO status, IV fluids, and IV hydromorphone for pain. Her symptoms improved over several days, allowing advancement to a regular diet with minimal pain. An abdominal ultrasound showed no biliary or pancreatic duct dilation, and the ERCP team recommended no intervention during this admission. She was discharged home with a short course of oral hydromorphone for breakthrough pain, continuation of home medications including ranitidine and psychiatric drugs, and new Miralax for constipation. Follow-up with GI specialists was arranged to address recurrent abdominal pain episodes. Additional issues noted during admission included anal fissure with rectal bleeding, constipation, a nonspecific rash, mild hypotension, and a cardiac dysrhythmia, all managed supportively.
